A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DP human pose estimation study, with matching architecture and original MPII experiments. All substantive text, equations, tables, figures, and v3's supplementary material are readable. v1 has no separately designated appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original MPII experiments comparing non-private training, DP-SGD, and projected DP-SGD across training strategies, clipping thresholds, and privacy budgets (Tables 1–3 and Figure 1).

after.justification: v3 retains original MPII results and adds feature-private and hybrid-method experiments, blurred-image controls, Human-Art evaluations, and qualitative predictions, including supplementary results.

M1.justification: v3 adds Feature DP-SGD and a hybrid feature-projective method. Training combines unperturbed gradients from blurred public features with clipped, noisy raw-image gradients, optionally projected into the public gradient subspace (Equations 7–11 and Algorithm 1). The TinyViT coordinate-classification architecture and original projection method remain.

E1.justification: COCO pretraining and MPII evaluation remain. v3 adds Human-Art experiments covering natural and artistic imagery, extending evaluation to stylized human appearances and poses absent from v1's evaluation coverage (Experiments and supplementary Tables 6–9).

E2.justification: The MPII comparison expands from non-private training, vanilla DP-SGD, and projected DP-SGD to include standalone Feature DP-SGD and public-features-only training controls (v3 Tables 1 and 4). These are explicitly evaluated alongside the new hybrid method, rather than merely cited.

E3.justification: The reported privacy-budget sweep narrows from ε={0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1,3,5,7} to ε={0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, removing the relaxed-budget evaluation regime. v3 also introduces blurred-image-only controls. The existing 25-epoch budget, input resolution, clipping thresholds, RDP accounting, and projection settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds component comparisons testing feature privacy alone versus projection alone and their combination, plus controls examining what blurred public features retain. Figures 3–4 add qualitative pose comparisons and raw-versus-blurred examples. v1's analyses principally examined projection, clipping, privacy budgets, and initialization.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run error bars. The reported accuracy means do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All shared ε=0.2–0.8 rows in Tables 2–3 retain their numerical values; results at ε=1,3,5,7 are removed. v3 adds feature-private, hybrid, public-feature-only, Human-Art, and qualitative results. For example, Table 5 reports hybrid MPII finetuning accuracy of 82.62% at C=0.1, ε=0.8, while the abstract says 82.61%; this is a new-method result, not an updated original-method score.

T1.justification: v3 introduces a formal f-FDP definition and its (ε,δ) specialization, restricting neighboring records to those with identical public representations ψ(x) (Equation 6). This substantively changes the privacy assumptions for the added method. v1's separate L1-sensitivity definition and Gaussian calibration equations are removed; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The first-DP-HPE claim remains, but the central contribution shifts from projected DP-SGD and a novel lightweight architecture to feature privacy and the hybrid method. v3 adds claims of automatic protection for subjects and surrounding context, and makes hybrid performance the headline result; the retained architecture is no longer a principal novelty claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of feature/projection synergy, attributes projection underperformance to subspace reconstruction error interacting with noise, and discusses why whole-image blurring protects contextual information. Its supplement newly identifies Human-Art non-convergence and explains omission of low-utility settings. These extend and qualify v1's projection-centered interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the public-feature Gaussian blur kernel as 25×25 with standard deviation 10. It also clarifies that 'finetuning from scratch' uses COCO-pretrained weights while training all layers. Most existing implementation settings are relocated to the supplement rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v3 substantially extends positioning toward selective and feature differential privacy, discussing Shi et al. (2021) and Mahloujifar et al. (2025) as foundations for the new approach. It also adds discussion of realistic full-body anonymization and its limitations through the Hukkelås works, beyond v1's conventional anonymization discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, results narrative, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related-work subsections are merged, the architecture description moves ahead of projection, and implementation details and detailed results are organized into supplementary material. These changes restructure the retained narrative as well as accommodate new content.

P2.justification: v3 adds a pipeline diagram and qualitative image panels, expands Table 1 with public-feature controls, and introduces additional result tables. v1's nine-panel Figure 1 becomes v3 Figure 2 with additional method curves and a restricted ε axis. Detailed original tables move to the supplement within a substantially revised layout.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1's MPII-focused projection study, v3 improves experimental breadth and inspectability through component controls, Human-Art evaluation, and explicit hybrid pseudocode. However, Equation 6 restricts privacy to records sharing public features, while the text claims identical privacy constraints and complete raw-image protection. Public-feature-only finetuning also scores 83.61% (Table 1), above the hybrid's 82.62% (Table 5). These unresolved issues affect the central privacy-utility claim, preventing a reliable net quality judgment despite the substantial additions.
